summary: This informational document provides a framework for Layer 2 Provider Provisioned Virtual Private Networks. It is meant to help standardize protocols and mechanisms so that different L2VPN implementations can interoperate.

plainLanguage.summary: A phone company can give each customer a private line across its shared wires. This document is the big picture map that helps different makers build such services that work together.

questions: what is a provider edge router
subtitle: The reference models and building blocks for provider-run Layer 2 VPNs: point-to-point wires, emulated LANs and the pseudowires underneath.

tldr.problem: Service providers wanted to offer customers private Layer 2 connectivity over a shared MPLS or IP backbone, but different proposals used different terms and mechanisms, which made them hard to compare and to make interoperate.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC gives reference models and breaks any L2VPN into common parts: attachment circuits, pseudowires, forwarders, tunnels, encapsulation and signaling. It then shows how VPWS, VPLS and IPLS arrange them.
tldr.outcome: It is a framework only. It lays out the issues and how approaches relate, but does not select any particular approach.

sections.title: Scope and Kinds of L2VPN
sections.content:
This framework covers Layer 2 Provider Provisioned VPNs, meaning VPNs where the service provider takes part in managing and provisioning the VPN. It offers reference models and discusses functional components and the technical issues that matter for standards, including interworking and security. It tries to show how the approaches relate but does not choose one. Requirements are in RFC 4665.

There are two fundamentally different services. A Virtual Private Wire Service (VPWS) gives a point-to-point L2 service. A Virtual Private LAN Service (VPLS) emulates a LAN across a Wide Area Network, so its edge state scales like a LAN. A third possibility is an IP-only LAN-like service (IPLS).

VPLS emulates native multicast over a service that has none, which raises scalability issues. It may also add delay and be less reliable than a native LAN, and standard LAN control protocols may have scaling problems there.
sections.plainLanguage: There are two kinds of private service. One is a single private cable between two offices. The other makes many offices look like they share one room.

sections.title: Reference Models
sections.content:
In the VPWS model, customer edge (CE) devices attach to provider edge (PE) devices over attachment circuits. PEs are joined by a pseudowire inside a PSN tunnel across the backbone, which contains P routers. The PE maps between pseudowire and attachment circuit using only local information, namely the PW demultiplexor and the incoming or outgoing port.

In the VPLS model, a CE attaches through a bridge module in the VPLS-PE, which attaches through an Emulated LAN interface to an Emulated LAN. Inside, VPLS Forwarders joined by pseudowires form the LAN. A VPLS instance is a set of VPLS Forwarders, at most one per PE. At a minimum the bridge module must learn MAC addresses and age them out. The framework allows three models: one bridge module with one VPLS instance, one bridge module with several instances treated as VLANs, and several bridge modules each with one instance.

PE functions may also be split. The User-facing PE (U-PE) is closer to the customer, and the Network-facing PE (N-PE) is closer to the core. The forwarder in a VPWS-PE maps one attachment circuit to one pseudowire. In a VPLS-PE it is a Virtual Switching Instance (VSI) that maps many circuits to many pseudowires.
sections.plainLanguage: Each office plugs into a box at the phone company. The boxes talk to each other over shared lines. One box setup acts like a plain cable, and another acts like a shared office switch.

sections.title: Common Building Blocks
sections.content:
Every L2VPN carries frames from a CE through a PE, across the core, through another PE to a CE. Several parts do this.

  • Attachment circuit (AC): the circuit between CE and PE, such as a Frame Relay DLCI, an ATM VPI/VCI, an Ethernet port, a VLAN or a PPP connection. Setting up ACs is out of scope and left to each technology.
  • Pseudowire (PW): a relation between two PEs that carries frames between them. State is kept only at its two end PEs, not in P routers. PWs may be point-to-point, multipoint-to-point or point-to-multipoint.
  • Forwarder: the procedure that picks the PW for a frame arriving on an AC, and the AC for a frame arriving on a PW, using the incoming circuit, possibly the Layer 2 header, and possibly forwarding information.
  • Tunnel: carries one or more PWs between PEs. MPLS LSPs, L2TP tunnels, IPsec tunnels and MPLS-in-IP tunnels are examples. The tunnel needs a demultiplexor field so the egress PE can tell which PW a frame belongs to.

If a PW joins ACs of the same technology it provides homogeneous transport. Otherwise it is heterogeneous and needs interworking, which can be done by a CE, by a PE, or by IPLS. The setup protocol must make sure each end knows the remote AC's MTU. If MTUs differ, the PW is not allowed up, the larger side reduces its MTU, or both agree on fragmentation and reassembly.
sections.plainLanguage: The cable from your office to the phone company is the attachment circuit. The long-distance link between two phone company boxes is the pseudowire. A tunnel is the big pipe that can hold many of these links.

sections.title: Signaling and Provisioning
sections.content:
Signaling must hand out the demultiplexor, pick the forwarder at the remote PE through a Remote Forwarder Selector, support emulation of Layer 2 signaling, pass state changes and establish PW characteristics. Usually the egress PE chooses the demultiplexor value and tells the ingress PE. Point-to-point signaling can use LDP (RFC 3036) or L2TP (RFC 2661). Point-to-multipoint signaling can fit when many PWs share the same characteristics and selector, for example using BGP (RFC 1771) with route reflectors (RFC 2796).

For a VPWS, each forwarder binds exactly one AC to exactly one PW, so the frame's Layer 2 header plays no role in the forwarding decision. The RFC describes three provisioning models:

  • Two-sided: each PE is given the local AC, PW type and parameters, the remote PE's IP address and an identifier meaningful to the remote PE.
  • Single-sided: one PE is given the local AC, PW type and parameters and a globally unique remote AC identifier, and auto-discovery maps it to the remote PE.
  • Colored pools: ACs are grouped into pools with a color, and PWs are set up between like-colored pools, which easily yields a full mesh or hub and spoke.

Auto-discovery across service provider boundaries is required, which rules out piggybacking on the backbone's IGP. Inter-AS pseudowires need endpoints that can reach each other, a signaling protocol that crosses networks, and authentication with acceptable key distribution.
sections.plainLanguage: To connect two offices, the boxes need to agree on a label for the link. You can write the plan down on both ends, on one end only, or color-code the offices so every same-colored pair gets linked.

sections.title: VPLS Emulated LANs and IPLS
sections.content:
In a VPLS, a unicast frame is sent to only the one Forwarder that needs it when its location is known. Each Forwarder behaves as a Virtual Switch Instance (VSI) with a table mapping MAC addresses to PWs, built by source address learning. Frames with unknown or multicast destinations are sent to all other Forwarders. Unlike a standard bridge, a VPLS Forwarder learns source addresses only from PWs and not from its ACs, and Forwarders use a split horizon technique instead of a spanning tree.

Overlay topologies of pseudowires include a full mesh, a tree and a tree with a meshed highest level. In a full mesh, a frame received over a PW MUST NOT be forwarded over any other PW. Loop freedom in the overlay does not guarantee loop freedom in the customer LAN. A deployment needs n*(n-1) pseudowires between VPLS-PE routers, which creates scaling problems that hierarchy can address.

The IP-only LAN-like Service (IPLS) assumes the CEs are hosts or routers and carries only IP and supporting packets such as ICMP, ARP and Neighbor Discovery. Because each CE uses one MAC address on an AC, the PE can learn it through the control plane rather than the data plane, which allows hardware that cannot learn MAC addresses. An IPLS instance must have an IPLS-wide MTU.
sections.plainLanguage: A shared-room service works like a mail room: it learns which desk each person sits at, sends mail only to that desk when it knows, and shouts to everyone when it does not.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC splits security into three areas: the provider network, the provider-customer interface and the customer network. Within the provider network, a PE should not open a control connection with an arbitrary peer, and it should be configured with its peers or learn them from a trusted auto-configuration procedure. For connections between service providers, cryptographic authentication is advisable, such as the TCP MD5 option or IPsec, which gives greater assurance at greater cost. Limiting the processing rate of control traffic can reduce denial-of-service effects. A VPLS can be attacked with many frames that have multicast or unknown destinations, or with bogus source MAC addresses that fill the MAC tables and cause flooding.

At the provider-customer interface, existing Layer 2 mechanisms such as IEEE 802.1x apply. For the customer network, misconfiguration of a PE may join CEs that should be separate. L2VPN procedures give no authentication, integrity or privacy for customer traffic, so a customer who needs those must provide them, for example with IPsec.
sections.plainLanguage: The phone company has to make sure it only talks to its real partner boxes, and a prankster flooding the line should not break things. If you want your messages secret, you have to lock them yourself.

items.title: Full mesh
items.text: Every VSI has one point-to-point PW to every other VSI. A frame received over a PW must not be forwarded over any other PW.

items.title: Tree structured
items.text: Each VSI sits at a level and has at most one PW leading higher. A frame from a higher level may not go to a higher level.

items.title: Tree with meshed highest level
items.text: Several VSIs may be at the top, and they must be fully meshed. Frames from the same level cannot be sent to the same level.
